topic: Windows Agent 7.82 local IPC on port 5001 timing out on some Domain Controllers, plus Kubelet warnings on non-containerized hosts
product_area: Agent / Windows / local IPC (CMD API) / Remote Configuration / system-probe
environment: Agent upgraded in place from 7.76.3 to 7.82.2 (also tried 7.82.3)
Non-containerized Windows VMs with no Kubernetes or container runtime
Agent installed on a non-default drive
symptom_pattern: After upgrading from 7.76.3 to 7.82.x, system-probe starts very slowly on two hosts. The core agent logs repeated remote-config 'retrying the first update' errors with a growing consecutive-failure count, caused by connection attempts to the local CMD API port timing out. agent status, flare and the Tray app also fail on those hosts, although metrics are still reported normally. Separately, the Agent logs a Kubelet HTTPS-to-HTTP fallback warning every 30 minutes on Windows hosts that don't run containers. An identically configured Domain Controller in the same domain was unaffected.
root_cause: Per the customer, a misconfiguration in Windows Defender Firewall on the affected hosts was blocking local communication with the Datadog Agent. The Agent itself was healthy and listening. Local connections to the CMD API port hung until they timed out, with no SYN-ACK and no RST, which pointed to a host-level driver or firewall filter dropping the packets. Changing cmd_port or the Agent version did not help.
resolution_path: Customer first changed cmd_port, upgraded 7.82.2 to 7.82.3 and rebooted, with no improvement
The TSE reviewed the debug flare and found the Core Agent API starts listening, but connections to it fail seconds later, including from Agent subprocesses
The TSE asked for netstat, curl, firewall profile and antivirus status output, plus datadog.yaml and system-probe.yaml
The output showed the Agent bound and listening but every local connection hung for about 21 seconds and timed out, which indicates silently dropped loopback packets on the host
The TSE asked the customer to involve the owners of Windows Firewall and endpoint security and compare the broken hosts with a working Domain Controller
Engineering confirmed no Agent-side cause and no supported way to move the CMD API off TCP loopback on Windows. Changing cmd_port was the only knob
A diagnostic script was sent to run on a broken host and a known-good host in the same domain for comparison
The customer found and corrected the Windows Defender Firewall misconfiguration, and the issue was resolved
info_needed: Debug flare from an affected host
Whether anything differs between the affected and unaffected hosts (site, OU, EDR policy, GPO)
Listening-socket and connection-test output for the local CMD API port
Windows Firewall profile status and antivirus or endpoint product status
Output of a packet-drop capture script from one broken and one working host on the same day

qa_pairs.tse_question: Can you run netstat, curl against the local port, and collect firewall and antivirus status from the affected host?
qa_pairs.customer_answer: Customer supplied the outputs. The antivirus product query failed because the SecurityCenter2 namespace does not exist on Windows Server, so they sent Get-MpComputerStatus output instead.

qa_pairs.tse_question: What is different about the affected hosts compared with the other Domain Controllers that are fine (site, OU, EDR policy, GPO link)?
qa_pairs.customer_answer: Their team said there are no intentional differences, since the hosts are built from the same baseline with identical OU structure, GPOs and security policies. In one domain, one Domain Controller was affected and the other was not.

qa_pairs.tse_question: Please run the provided diagnostic script on a broken host and a working host in the same domain and send both outputs.
qa_pairs.customer_answer: Customer sent the outputs from both servers, then tested other Agent versions and found the last version without the error was 7.78.4. They later corrected that conclusion, saying the status and Tray problems persisted.

evidence: Impossible to reach Kubelet through HTTPS, fallback to HTTP, err=Kubelet connection check failed
retrying the first update of remote-config state

tse_approach.summary: The TSE used the debug flare and local diagnostics to show the Agent was healthy and listening, while local connections to the CMD API port were being silently dropped. They then steered the customer toward the host firewall and endpoint-security layer and brought in engineering, who confirmed there was no Agent-side cause. The customer found the firewall misconfiguration themselves.
steps: Reviewed the debug flare and identified that the local API starts but connections to it fail
Explained which functions depend on the local IPC port and which data paths are unaffected, to scope the impact
Requested netstat, curl, firewall profile and antivirus status output, plus the config files
Interpreted the output as silently dropped loopback packets and pointed to a firewall rule or endpoint filter
Said support was best effort for host networking and asked the customer to involve the firewall and endpoint security owners
Escalated to Windows Agent engineering, then relayed their findings and the lack of a supported workaround
Provided a read-only diagnostic script to run on a broken host and a working host for comparison
Kept the ticket open and pending while the customer tested further
key_questions: What is different about the affected hosts compared with the working Domain Controllers?
Can you run the netstat, curl and firewall status commands and attach the output?
Can you run the diagnostic script on both a broken and a working host on the same day?
